newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks stage modest Christmas rally.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks stage modest Christmas rally.

text.p: Tokyo stocks rebounded on Wednesday from a sharp tumble the previous day, helped by seasonal cheer on Wall Street, as investors hunted for bargains among blue-chip shares.
But brokers said the rally lacked real vigour and was accentuated by thin Christmas Day trade.

The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares recouped much of the ground it had lost on Tuesday on gloom about the Japanese economy, rising just over two percent in a blue chip-led technical bounce.
A series of slides had left global issues such as shares in big exporters looking attractively priced.
With Wednesday being the last trading day for settlement this year, some players were also keen to buy up shares to cover their positions after the market's recent steep drop.

The Nikkei closed with solid gains, up 387.70 points or 2.02 percent at 19,549.41. The index fell 528.75 points or 2.69 percent on Tuesday to a 12-month low of 19,161.71, depressed by concerns about the impact of fiscal tightening next year on Japan's fledgling economic recovery.
The broader TOPIX index closed up 20.98 points or 1.45 percent at 1,469.43.
Japan's stock market had a full-day trading session on Wednesday but activity was thinned by the absence of foreign brokers celebrating Christmas Day.
With volume light, a Christmas Eve rally on Wall Street to a near-record closing high overnight helped to give the market a mild lift early on, brokers said.

Stocks have taken a battering since the government confirmed last week that it will raise Japan's consumption tax next April and end special income tax cuts as part of a drive to rein in government borrowing.
Brokers are worried that the fiscal tightening could choke off Japan's economic recovery and hurt corporate profits.
A government plan for "Big Bang" liberalisation of financial markets has also weighed on financial institutions which are still struggling to clean up bad loan problems.
"I am a bit disappointed by today's rebound after the plunge yesterday," Kokusai Securities analyst Kenzo Doi said, citing a lack of buyers at higher level to give the recovery momentum.
A trader at a foreign brokerage echoed his view, saying the recovery was not as vigorous as the rise in stock indices suggested.

Several hundred stocks, including construction, paper/pulp and raw materials issues, hit new lows for the year on Wednesday, suggesting that smaller shares are still under pressure despite the interest in the blue-chip components of the Nikkei average, he said.
Strong sectors included telecommunications, precision instruments and pharmaceuticals. Toyota Motor was one of the blue chips being bargain-hunted, brokers said.

Some analysts said the Nikkei would consolidate at the 19,000-20,000 level for a while. But others said it would remain vulnerable due to lack of fresh news to support the market before the end of the year.
